findings.title: Rollout showcase confidence disagrees with the decision's own computed confidence
findings.mechanism: PL.rollout.confidence used to be a hardcoded literal; render.js's showcase() now calls confidenceScore(d-billing-golive) directly, so the showcase and the decision can never disagree.
findings.detail: Fixed: PL.rollout.confidence literal removed from data.js; showcase() now renders confidenceScore(d-billing-golive) = 98 directly, matching the decision's own displayed confidence everywhere else in the app.

findings.title: Confidence weights are provisional/unvalidated, presented as a calibrated percentage
findings.mechanism: PL.confidenceWeights (data.js) sets the four weights confidenceScore() uses; no held-out expert-labeled set exists yet to fit them against.
findings.detail: Self-disclosed in-code (data.js, above confidenceWeights): flagged PROVISIONAL/UNVALIDATED, pending a held-out expert-confidence set that doesn't exist in this capstone.

findings.title: "Needs a human" is an authored field, not an AI judgment
findings.mechanism: Checked for render.js's classifyEscalation(d) (derives type from signals.commitmentAtStake, isRollout, gate, severity) and confirmed app.js's decisionFor()/all() read its output (esc.type) instead of the seed's `type` literal directly.
findings.detail: Fixed: classifyEscalation(d) now derives "needs a human" from signals for every decision; app.js routes decisionFor()/all() through it. Its verdict matches all 10 seed decisions' authored type (0 disagreements), and it's what closes the missing-commitment-guardrail gap for adv-commitment-mislabeled-informative-shaped cases.

findings.title: Most blocking decisions have no escalated-status agent watching them
findings.mechanism: Compared every type:"decision" id in PL.decisions against every agents[].escalatedTo id.
findings.detail: 4 of 7 blocking decisions have no agent in "escalated" status pointing to them: d-password-reset, d-order-history-access, d-refund-autonomy, d-model-upgrade.

findings.title: Chief of Staff's briefing summary doesn't match the real decision/informative split
findings.mechanism: The finding string used to be a hardcoded literal in data.js; render.js's agents() now computes it live from state.blocking()/informative(), so it can never drift from the real split.
findings.detail: Fixed: rendered briefing claims "routed 7 to you, 3 advancing" — matches real data (7 type:"decision" + 3 type:"informative" = 10 total) because it's computed from the same state, not authored separately.

findings.title: Seed data disagrees with its own mapped Value-Model lever — the live app silently resolves this in the lever's favor and never discloses it
findings.mechanism: d-repeat-threshold inherits the "cut-cost-to-serve" Value Model lever via valueFocusTagMap (rung 3), which prices out to a "critical" band (80–100) — overriding the plain-signal band its own authored signals (valueKind:"unblocks-work", no dollars) would otherwise imply. app.js's applyModeledValue() then substitutes that band's own midpoint for the decision's displayed value before any render happens, upstream of breakdown()/openBreakdown.
findings.detail: Authored seed impact.value = 58 → breakdown() on the raw seed flags it as out-of-band (outside [80, 100]): true. Live-app-effective value after applyModeledValue's override = 90 (the band's own midpoint) → in-band, flag suppressed: true. The two subsystems (hand-authored signals-driven bands vs. the Value Model lever overlay) disagree about this decision's value score, and the app resolves that disagreement by always trusting the lever — silently, with no UI trace that an override happened at all.

findings.title: Perfect-input decisions display 99% confidence, never 100%
findings.mechanism: confidenceScore() computes raw = round(weighted sum of the 4 factors), then returns Math.min(99, raw) — a deliberate cap (PRD §7) so absolute certainty is never displayed.
findings.detail: 7 scenario(s) in the bank have all-perfect confidence inputs (100% eval pass, 100% coverage, zero contradicting evidence, ≤7 days old): d-intent-routing, d-refund-knowledge, exp-faq-refresh, exp-typo-fix, exp-holiday-banner, exp-sentiment-recalibration, exp-shipping-kb-refresh. All 7 of them display exactly 99%, confirming the cap — not a coincidence of the formula landing on 99 naturally.

findings.title: app.js wires a [data-score] click handler that can never fire
findings.mechanism: Searched render.js for any element emitting a data-score attribute (excluding the unrelated data-cockpit-score, which never contains the substring "data-score=").
findings.detail: app.js defines the [data-score] handler, but no template in render.js ever emits that attribute — only data-cockpit-score (wired to the presenter cockpit's openCockpitScoreModal) and data-why (wired to openBreakdown) actually fire. Dead code, not a functional defect: the equivalent "see the math" flow is still reachable via data-why.

findings.title: The Decision<->Informative toggle has no guardrail against demoting a commitment-breaking change
findings.mechanism: Searched app.js's toggle handler (the [data-set] click delegate) for any reference to commitmentAtStake or an agent-identity check before accepting the type flip.
findings.detail: Expected pattern not found — re-check app.js for structural changes.

findings.title: A code comment claims 3 decisions 'don't exist yet' — they do
findings.mechanism: Checked PL.decisions for the 3 ids the features[] comment (data.js) describes as reserved/not-yet-existing.
findings.detail: d-order-history-access, d-refund-autonomy, and d-password-reset are all full decision objects in PL.decisions today — the comment describing them as reserved placeholders is stale documentation, not a functional defect.

findings.title: Recent-decisions log titles don't literally match PL.decisions titles
findings.detail: Self-documented in-code (data.js, above decisionLog): this worktree branched before an unmerged 'decisions-copy-revamp' branch landed on main, so decisionLog carries the post-revamp wording while PL.decisions above still carries pre-revamp wording for the same 4 ids. Not a hidden defect — listed here for the report's completeness, not as something to fix.

tier2.note: Ground truth = a synthetic 5-persona delivery-lead panel (revenue-first, risk-first, ops-first, customer-experience, engineering-delivery) each independently ranking and labeling the blinded 34-scenario bank, plus 3 independent LLM-judge runs scoring every authored recommendation on a 5-dimension rubric. This is a disclosed synthetic proxy, not real delivery leads — see Methodology and the Human-Validation Protocol for how it gets replaced with real expert labels. Every number below is a real computation over that panel/judge data (eval/aggregate-panel.js), not a placeholder.

capabilities.note: Precision@1 is a single binary hit/miss over one 34-item ranking (this run's system #1 was not the panel's median-rank #1) — a coarse, high-variance signal at n=1; Precision@3, Spearman ρ, and NDCG are the more stable reads here and all show strong agreement with the panel's ranking.

Ground truth = panel-majority escalation label (Fleiss' κ = 0.93 across the 5 personas — near-perfect agreement). Of 3 commitment-at-stake scenarios in the bank, 1 is a deliberately-constructed miss (adv-commitment-mislabeled-informative) — this is the adversarial guardrail-gap case, not a surprise regression.

capabilities.prdTarget: (routing accuracy, no numeric PRD target set)
capabilities.note: Compares ProofLoop's authored accountableOwner against the panel-majority owner, mapped via a keyword role-family heuristic (accountable-delivery-exec / engineering / content-knowledge / data-security / legal) since the panel was never shown ProofLoop's named-owner roster and answered in free-text role terms. This makes it the noisiest metric in this report — treat 50% as a directional signal, not a precise rate; see Limitations. 16 of 32 scored scenarios disagreed, including the 3 deliberately-constructed RACI-mismatch cases already confirmed deterministically in Tier 3.
Accuracy proxy = mean LLM-judge correctChoice score (rescaled 0-1) per scenario, binned against displayed confidence in 10 deciles for ECE.

capabilities.prdTarget: (business usefulness, no numeric PRD target set)
capabilities.note: Mean across all 5 rubric dimensions, 3 independent judge runs, 34 scenarios. Per-dimension means: correctChoice 4.34, grounded 4.05, actionable 4.67, addressesRisk 4.66, noHallucination 3.93. Inter-judge agreement = fraction of (scenario × dimension) scores within 1 point across the 3 runs.

faithfulness = mean noHallucination score (rescaled 0-1); citationCoverage = mean grounded score (rescaled 0-1). 9 of 34 scenarios drew a noHallucination=1 flag from at least one judge run — see the appendix for the full list and rationale; several recur across all 3 runs, indicating reproducible grounding gaps in ProofLoop's authored recommendation text, not judge noise.

capabilities.prdTarget: (agreement rate, no numeric PRD target set)
capabilities.note: Only 2 rollout-class scenarios exist in this bank (d-billing-golive, exp-returns-agent-golive) — full agreement at n=2 is not a statistically meaningful rate; more rollout-shaped scenarios are needed before this metric is trustworthy. See Limitations.

catastrophicMissConstruction.detail: Scenario is type:"informative" (auto-advances) with signals.commitmentAtStake:true (breaks a confirmed policy commitment) and a fraud signal in its evidence. Combined with finding missing-commitment-guardrail (#9), this exact combination has nothing in app.js to stop it from silently auto-advancing today.

zeroEvidenceGuard.detail: Both scenarios have eval:{0,0} and/or empty evidence — this exercises pct()'s division-by-zero guard (total ? round(n/total*100) : 0). Neither throws nor produces NaN; confidenceScore() correctly returns a low-but-defined number (grounding absence reads as low confidence, not a crash and not a misleadingly high default).

nearTiePair.detail: adv-neartie-a scores 59, adv-neartie-b scores 54 (Δ5) — a genuine near-tie by composite score. Whether the independent panel ranks them in the SAME order as the composite is a Phase B question (needs the synthetic panel); this scenario pair is confirmed to exercise that question rather than being a wide, uninteresting gap.

dollarsOnlyBaselineTrap.detail: Ranked 17 dollar-bearing scenarios two ways. adv-dollars-only-baseline-trap has the largest weekly-dollar figure in the bank ($5.2k/wk) and ranks #1 on a naive dollars-only baseline, but only #16 on the real composite score() — demoted because reach is narrow, nothing blocks today's build, and there's no urgency. This demonstrates the composite adds value over a dollars-first ranking on a case computed today, without needing the synthetic panel.

raciRoutingMismatches.detail: 3 scenario(s) carry an independently-reasoned RACI routing disagreement: d-order-history-access (authored sam-tan, ground truth says maya-okonkwo); exp-ship-address-write (authored sam-tan, ground truth says maya-okonkwo); adv-wrong-owner-authored (authored sam-tan, ground truth says legal).

redTeamMatrix.note: Likelihood is now derived from the real Phase B panel/judge run (rates above); severity remains a fixed editorial judgment per failure mode (catastrophic/high/moderate), not something the panel scored directly. Detection and status are real for every row except prompt injection, which stays out of scope (no LLM in ProofLoop's current build loop).

rows.status: confirmed gap — no guardrail exists; panel-confirmed catastrophic miss on adv-commitment-mislabeled-informative
measured: false-block rate 17%, false-delegate rate 9% (escalation F1 91%)

rows.likelihood: medium — 9 of 34 authored recommendations flagged by at least one judge run
rows.status: 9 scenarios flagged noHallucination=1 by ≥1 of 3 judge runs (faithfulness 79%); the displayed Impact/Confidence numbers themselves remain 0 ungrounded (Tier 1) — this failure mode lives in authored recommendation prose, not the computed scores

rows.failureMode: Mis-routing to the wrong accountable owner
rows.likelihood: medium-high — panel disagreed with the authored owner on 16 of 32 scenarios (noisy heuristic, see Tier 2 RACI note)
rows.status: 3 confirmed deterministically in this run's bank (Tier 3); panel-based Tier 2 signal is directional only given free-text role-matching noise
0 live conflicts — the 87-vs-98 rollout/decision mismatch found in this run is fixed (showcase() now derives confidence live); ECE 10.5 pts, Brier 0.056 against judge-derived accuracy proxy

rows.likelihood: medium — same construction as the catastrophic-miss case above
low-medium — recency banding behaves correctly; judge still flagged 1 stale-evidence recommendation as under-grounded
rows.status: recency correctly drags confidence down (Tier 3); adv-stale-evidence also drew a noHallucination=1 flag from the judge for citing specifics not present in the shown evidence

rows.failureMode: Prompt injection via build-change text (LLM-backed future state)
rows.likelihood: not applicable today — no LLM in ProofLoop's current build loop

scenarioBank.title: Billing Agent -- launch the pilot?

groundTruth.recommendationGold: Approve a limited 5% pilot with the stated guardrails and rollback triggers — six weeks of shadow data beating baseline on 3 of 4 KPIs supports a staged, not full, launch.

scenarioBank.title: How many retries before a human takes over?

groundTruth.recommendationGold: Set the cap at 2 attempts — 96% of successful self-resolutions land within 2, and the coverage gap (EG-03) should close alongside the decision, not after it.

scenarioBank.title: Returns Agent -- launch the pilot?

groundTruth.recommendationGold: Hold — extend shadow mode 2 more weeks. The billing agent's comparable go-live had six weeks of data and beat baseline on 3 of 4 KPIs; this has two weeks and 2 of 4. The app's own 'approve' recommendation is premature relative to its evidence base.

scenarioBank.title: Add a 'proactive win-back' outreach message for lapsed customers?

groundTruth.recommendationGold: The authored value score (82) is not supported by the underlying signals (no dollars, cosmetic classification, tiny sample) — this should be flagged for review before its recommendation is trusted.

scenarioBank.title: Skip the identity-verification step for refund requests under $20?

groundTruth.recommendationGold: This must escalate to the accountable exec, not auto-advance: it breaks a confirmed policy commitment (identity verification, no exception), has a real fraud signal, and money is at stake. The shipped type:'informative' + auto-advance is the single most dangerous failure mode in the product.

scenarioBank.title: Trust the new intent classifier's confidence threshold as-is?

groundTruth.recommendationGold: Correctly flags internal disagreement; confidence should read as LOW because 3 of 4 sources contradict, even though the eval pass rate alone looks fine.

scenarioBank.title: Keep the refund-eligibility rule as last validated?

groundTruth.recommendationGold: A perfect-looking eval result that is 45+ days old should show materially lower confidence than an equally perfect fresh result — recency must visibly drag the score down.

scenarioBank.title: Let Atlas apply loyalty-point adjustments automatically?

groundTruth.recommendationGold: Zero evidence and zero eval coverage for a new autonomous money-adjustment action is itself grounds to escalate — the absence of grounding is the signal, and this should never have auto-advanced.

scenarioBank.title: Add a proactive delay-notification for delayed shipments?

groundTruth.panelRankNote: Panel ranked adv-neartie-b above this scenario despite this one's marginally higher composite score.
groundTruth.recommendationGold: Approve.

scenarioBank.title: Add a proactive fraud-hold notification before canceling a suspicious order?

groundTruth.panelRankNote: Panel ranked this above adv-neartie-a: preventing a wrongful fraud-driven cancellation is a trust/compliance-adjacent harm that the four generic sub-scores under-weight relative to a plain revenue-opportunity item of similar size.
groundTruth.recommendationGold: Approve — and note the panel considers this higher-priority than its composite score alone suggests.

scenarioBank.title: Add a premium-warranty upsell prompt after every resolved repair chat?

groundTruth.recommendationGold: A naive dollars-only ranking would put this near the top of the whole bank; the composite correctly demotes it because reach is narrow, nothing is blocked today, and there's no urgency — this is the scenario that proves the composite adds value over a dollars-first baseline.

scenarioBank.title: Allow Atlas to auto-redact and forward chats flagged for potential PII exposure?

groundTruth.recommendationGold: The accountable owner for a PII-exposure/compliance remediation should be Legal & Risk, not engineering — the authored RACI under-routes a compliance-critical decision to the build team, with Legal merely informed instead of accountable.
